description: CBCG publishes payment-system volumes (RTGS/DNS/IPS) and, apparently, payment-services statistics, but no card-scheme-level, acquiring-level or POS/ATM-terminal-estate breakdown surfaced in this cell.

This cell maps CBCG as publisher but not the individual banks'/PSPs' own investor-relations and disclosure pages, which are where Pillar 3 disclosures, shareholder-assembly materials and press releases actually live.
No non-CBCG archival/mirroring source was identified for withdrawn or superseded CBCG documents; CBCG appears to overwrite or move publication pages.
The English (/en/) mirror covers publications well but registers, tariffs and statistics appear predominantly Montenegrin-only; some /eng/ paths exist inconsistently.
Publication cadence and exact release dates (statistical publication calendar) were referenced but the calendar page itself was not located in this pass.

Of the 11 licensed banks in the CBCG register, a self-published reports page was located for 10 (CKB, Hipotekarna, Erste, NLB, Addiko, Prva, Lovćen, Adriatic, Universal Capital, Zapad, Ziraat). No page-level verification was done for any bank's full year-depth, and no scouting was done for banks in liquidation/wind-down or for branches of foreign banks.

General assembly / skupština akcionara materials (agendas, decisions, dividend and capital resolutions) were only confirmed for Hipotekarna banka. Other banks' assembly notices were not located in this pass.

Almost all primary documents are Serbian/Montenegrin only; English versions are sporadic (Erste: one 2015 report; NLB and UCB and Adriatic have partial EN locales). Some Erste documents were described as Cyrillic script while most Montenegrin material is Latin.

Year-depth per bank site is uneven and only partly observed (Hipotekarna 2007+, Erste 2009+, Addiko 2011+, Ziraat 2015+, NLB visibly only 2022+ before 'Show more' expansion). JS accordions may hide older years from a plain HTTP crawl.
Bank-issued press-release / news channels were confirmed only for Universal Capital and Hipotekarna in this pass, although the topic scope includes press releases.
robots.txt, ToS and rate-limit posture were not inspected for any bank domain in this pass.
The single most important source in this cell (CRPS public search) could not be retrieved in-session due to a TLS error.
No confirmed lawful, scalable channel for obtaining filed annual accounts of unlisted ME banks, payment institutions and vendor subsidiaries.
A new Zakon o računovodstvu (Sl. list CG 84/2025, in force 8 Aug 2025) postdates most of the filing-procedure material found, which is largely 2020-2021 vintage.
data.gov.me was identified but its actual catalogue was not enumerated for registry/tax/statistics datasets.

Other statutory registers likely relevant to payments actors were not explored in this slice: registar zaloga (pledges), registar neprofitnih organizacija, the Ministry of Finance auditor register, and the Central Depository Agency (CDA) shareholder register for joint-stock banks.

Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB), the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF), EU4Business/EFSE and the Regional Cooperation Council were not searched in this pass, although they fund and assess Montenegrin financial intermediaries and SME lending.

No payments-specific supranational assessor was located for Montenegro beyond the 2015 World Bank FSAP technical note — e.g. CPMI/BIS red-book style coverage, or SEPA/EPC-side accession documentation assessing Montenegrin scheme compliance.

Candidates in this cell are overwhelmingly PDF/HTML narrative. Machine-readable series (IMF FSI database, World Bank Global Financial Development / Findex, EBRD Banking Environment and Performance) were not explicitly enumerated in this pass.
No sr-language primary document from any supranational assessor was found; local-language coverage of this cell rests on media and EU-info relays only.

Several large PDFs (EC enlargement document-download endpoints, EBRD dam/ asset paths, IMF media source-pdf paths) use rotating or CDN-style URLs that may change between publication cycles; none were fetch-tested in this pass.
No Albanian-language Montenegrin media were searched or found, despite a significant Albanian-speaking population in Ulcinj/Malesija and MINA operating an Albanian service.

The cell found general and business press but no broadcast/video-first or podcast sources beyond RTCG's text site, and no social/professional channels (LinkedIn newsrooms, X accounts of bank PR desks and financial journalists) where appointments and deals often break first.

Only RTCG and Monitor were found to offer deep, systematically addressable archives (numeric article ids; PDF back-issues). For most portals the historical depth and archive URL structure are unknown.

Press coverage found is heavily weighted to sector-level profit aggregates derived from CBCG data. Individual-bank annual reports, investor-relations material and AGM/shareholder items were barely represented in media coverage.

Substantial republication overlap was observed across CdM, Aktuelno, Kodex and Borba, much of it likely originating from the MINA wire, but the originating outlet could not be determined from search snippets.

Career/vacancy channels are unmapped for NLB Banka Podgorica, Hipotekarna banka, Erste Bank Montenegro, Lovćen banka, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Ziraat Bank Montenegro and the Central Bank's own recruitment page.

Non-bank payment actors are entirely unmapped in this cell: licensed payment institutions and e-money issuers, card processors, ATM/POS acquirers/deployers and PSPs operating in ME. Their hiring and conference presence is arguably a sharper signal than bank hiring.

Conference sponsor and exhibitor rosters were identified at the site level but no individual sponsor list was actually retrieved for any ME event (INFINTECH sponsor page, IT SPOT sponsor tiers, MFM partners). Only Technobank's general sponsor (Payten) was observed via media coverage.

Wider-Balkans events beyond Technobank and Balkan Payment Forum were not swept — e.g. Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Albanian and North Macedonian banking-technology conferences and national digital-banking awards where ME banks or their group parents (OTP, NLB, Erste) appear.
No compliant substitute for LinkedIn hiring data has been identified (e.g. licensed job-posting datasets, Google Jobs structured data, or bank ATS endpoints exposing JSON).

The local-language glossary for this cell is built but untested against boolean job-board search: terms used include oglas za posao, slobodna radna mjesta, karijera, otvorene pozicije, platni promet, kartično poslovanje, digitalno bankarstvo, hakaton, takmičenje, nagrada, priznanje, sponzori, izlagači, konferencija, klaster. Not yet exercised: 'sistem osnovnog bankarstva'/'core banking' English-in-local usage, 'instant plaćanja', 'mobilno bankarstvo', 'PSD2 usklađenost', 'procesiranje kartica', 'bankomat/POS terminali'.
AZZK decision archive structure was inferred from year-index URLs and search snippets; the full year coverage (how far back listings go, whether pre-2013 decisions are archived) is unconfirmed.
No per-institution complaint statistics identified anywhere in the public domain for Montenegrin banks and payment institutions.
Enforcement-agent (javni izvršitelji) and their chamber, plus notary/enforcement notices, were not searched; these carry bank foreclosure and debt-enforcement volumes.
Official Gazette (Službeni list Crne Gore, sluzbenilist.me) was not directly searched, although it is the authoritative publication venue for the interchange law and for some agency acts.

European Commission Montenegro country reports (chapters 8 Competition, 28 Consumer and health protection, 4 Free movement of capital) were not fetched, though they audit enforcement performance annually in English.
Montenegrin business/investigative media coverage of bank complaints, fee increases and competition cases (Vijesti, Pobjeda, Dan, CIN-CG, Bankar.me) was not scouted in this cell.

Wayback coverage depth for individual ME bank domains (ckb.me, nlb.me, hipotekarnabanka.com, lovcenbanka.me, adriaticbank.com, universalcapitalbank.me, prvabankacg.com) was not enumerated in this run.
No national digital library / legal-deposit web archive for Montenegro was searched (analogous to national library web archiving programmes elsewhere).
EU/ECB-level aggregators (ECB Data Portal, EBA risk dashboards, Eurostat, EBRD/World Bank Global Findex and country diagnostics) were not enumerated for ME banking coverage.
The most authoritative independent commentary (Moody's, S&P, Fitch, Scope, EMIS, Cbonds) is registration- or subscription-gated, so no verified full-text collection method exists without procurement.
Montenegrin sources exist in both Latin and Cyrillic script and under both 'crnogorski' and 'srpski' labelling; only Latin-script sr queries were run this session.
CRPI / scmnreporting.me — the presumed official mechanism for storing regulated information — could not be entered in this pass (bare shell, cert-alias mismatch, 404 at reporting-portal root).

The exchange symbol index reports ~416 symbols but paginates; only the first ~20 were observed. The full set of bank and financial-institution issuers (equity symbols plus bank-issued bonds such as OB17-A, 1PBO1, 1NKBA, INBA) has not been enumerated, and symbol-to-legal-entity mapping is unconfirmed for most.

IR/disclosure sections were confirmed in detail only for Hipotekarna banka and CKB (and partially Prva banka). Lovćen banka, NLB Banka Podgorica, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Zapad banka, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat and others were identified as market actors but their listing status and issuer-disclosure pages were not individually verified.

The seed term 'obavještenje o značajnom događaju' (material-event notice) did not surface a dedicated exchange or regulator section under that exact label. The operative Montenegrin terminology used in practice (e.g. 'propisane informacije', 'unutrašnja informacija', 'informacije koje se objavljuju', 'značajno učešće') has not been pinned to actual publication surfaces.
No back-series strategy exists for exchange announcements or monthly bulletins; the site offers no visible archive index and news IDs are not densely enumerable.
With CKDD shareholder lists request-gated and no visible major-holdings notification feed, threshold-crossing and change-of-control events in listed banks may go undetected between annual reports.

All observed sources used Latin-script Montenegrin/Serbian; no Cyrillic variants were tested, and diacritic-insensitive matching (Lovcen/Lovćen, izvjestaj/izvještaj, Hipotekarna/HIPOTEKARNA) was not systematically validated.

Three registered payment institutions (Prestopay d.o.o., Business Integration and Business Intelligence d.o.o., and to a lesser extent Moneta MNE) have no located web presence; only their CBCG register PDFs describe them.
No interchange-fee / merchant-service-charge disclosure source identified for Montenegro (no equivalent of an EU IFR interchange publication was found).
Montenegrin-Cyrillic and alternative transliteration variants (e.g. 'платна институција', 'електронски новац') were not exercised in this pass; all local-language searching used Latin script.
Public-procurement and tender sources were not scouted, though bank/state tenders for POS, ATM and processing services are a strong indirect reveal of processor market share and contract renewals.
EU/EEA passported PSPs and e-money issuers serving Montenegrin customers cross-border (post-SEPA) are not covered by any ME register identified here.
Acquirer/processor layer for ME (who processes POS/e-commerce acquiring for the 11 banks) is not mapped; no vendor or processing-centre source identified in this pass.
The CBCG instant-payment scheme rulebook / operating rules and the decision setting caps and fee ceilings ('Odluka'/'Pravila rada platnog sistema') were not located as specific documents.
Official Gazette of Montenegro (Službeni list Crne Gore) was not covered in this slice despite being the authoritative publication venue for payment-system law and CBCG decisions.
Card/POS/ATM and e-money statistics for ME were not pinned to a specific dataset URL; only the parent statistics branch was located.
No Montenegrin-language material was found from Visa or Mastercard directly about ME beyond the mastercard.rs Google Pay page; local-language scheme communications are effectively absent.

The full roster of CBCG-licensed non-bank payment institutions, e-money institutions, registered AISPs and their agents was not enumerated — only Presto and (per its own claim) 2bi/Digitalni Kiosk were identified by name.

App-store release-note history was identified as a source type but only for Digitalni Kiosk; no systematic ME-storefront sweep of payment/wallet apps (Presto, bank apps, parking/transit apps, crypto wallets) was performed.

Merchant-side POS/ISV landscape only partially mapped (eFiskal, Sekas, Pošta CG PostFiskal, Telekom AdeoPOS/Pantheon). The Tax Administration's list of approved e-fiscalisation software providers was not located.
No Albanian-language coverage attempted, despite a significant Albanian-speaking population in Ulcinj/Tuzi where merchant-facing marketing may run in Albanian.
Funding-round announcements for Montenegrin payment startups were not found for any period; it is unclear whether none occurred or whether they are simply not published in indexed sources.
No confirmed machine-readable access path (API, bulk export, RSS, or stable notice-URL pattern) into CEJN, the mandatory national portal.
Only CBCG and Pošta Crne Gore were pinned down as individual contracting authorities. The rest of the payment-relevant buyer set is unenumerated.
No CPV-code mapping was established for the ME/banking-payments intersection, and no glossary of the noisy terms was validated against real notice text.
Unknown how far back CEJN's public archive reaches and whether pre-2019 notices from the old UJN portal (ujn.gov.me / portal.ujn.gov.me) remain retrievable.
Low-value 'jednostavne nabavke' (simple procurements, governed by a separate pravilnik) and direct negotiated awards may sit outside the main notice stream.
IFI-financed procurement executed by ME clients is split across ECEPP, World Bank STEP/Finances One, and the national portal, with no confirmed way to join records across them.

Card personalisation, card issuing/processing bureaus and switch vendors serving ME (beyond Payten/Bankart) are unmapped — e.g. who processes for Hipotekarna, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Adriatic and Ziraat ME.

No site-scoped crawl was performed on the vendor domains identified (payten.com, printecgroup.com, see.asseco.com, halcom.com, bankart.si, plus ME integrators), so their full ME reference inventories remain unenumerated.

Montenegrin-specific orthography and alias variants were only partially exercised (cnr vs sr; 'rješenje' vs 'rešenje'; 'sprječavanje' vs 'sprečavanje'; Latin vs Cyrillic; CKB/Crnogorska komercijalna banka/OTP; NLB Banka Podgorica/NLB Banka Crna Gora/Montenegrobanka).

Vendor-side traces embedded in technical artefacts (mobile app package namespaces, SDK strings, e-banking login page footers, TLS certificate SANs, DNS/MX records of ME bank domains) were identified conceptually but not systematically collected.
Vendor-side evidence in parent-group reporting (OTP Group for CKB, NLB Group for NLB Podgorica, Erste Group, Addiko Group, Ziraat) was not sampled in this cell.
Hipotekarna banka's parent AikGroup/AIK Banka has no confirmed English IR page located; only the Serbian corporate 'O nama' page and the securities-commission register were found.

Payments-specific KPIs (card issuing/acquiring volumes, POS/ATM estate, instant payments) inside group reporting were only partially covered - ASEE/Payten found, but card schemes' and processors' group reporting mentioning Montenegro (e.g. Nexi, Worldline, Visa/Mastercard CEE commentary) was not searched.
Parent-group home languages other than English were only lightly probed (Hungarian for OTP, Slovenian for NLB, German for Erste/Addiko, Polish for ASEE, Turkish for Ziraat).
Home-market regulated news services (BSE/BET Budapest, Ljubljana SE SEOnet, Vienna SE, Warsaw ESPI/EBI) were not enumerated as machine-readable disclosure feeds.
Historical depth was not established: only recent (2021-2026) group documents were sighted, so a multi-year Montenegro segment time series is not yet secured.

AmCham Montenegro's exact member-directory and position-paper URLs were not pinned down; the homepage confirms both exist but the site uses two competing path schemes (amcham.me/en/... and www.amcham.me/...) and legacy paths such as /advocacy/ now 404.
MFIC White Book and Banking Committee pages could not be read (403).
No association-side source located for microfinance institutions, leasing companies, or payment institutions/e-money issuers licensed in Montenegro.
The historical depth of UBCG's Bankar magazine archive and of the Glasnik PDF archive was not established; only recent issues and two sample PDFs were observed.
Several association sites (ubcg.info, komora.me, ictcortex.me, nbocg.me) serve parallel sr and en versions, but it was not established whether the English versions are complete or partial mirrors.
